item.title: Automatic Certified Differentiation in Lean
item.description: arXiv:2610.36396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automatic differentiation (the automatic computation of numerical function derivatives) has many applications, especially in scientific computing and machine learning. Several approaches to automate the calculation of derivatives have been presented. Common challenges facing those approaches include (1) having to define derivative rules for different classes of functions, (2) having to manipulate program symbols to understand the semantics of the function being differentiated, and construct the derivative function, and (3), more importantly, ensuring that the calculated derivative is correct. In this paper, we present an approach for automatic \emph{certified} differentiation using the Lean proof assistant. By certified, we mean a correctness certificate is computed together with the derivative function and a domain on which the derivative is guaranteed to be valid. Our approach leverages existing derivative theorems included in the Mathlib Lean library instead of having to define our own rules. We also utilize Lean metaprogramming to manipulate the symbolic structure of the input function, and to construct the derivative function. The correctness certificate is computed step-wise as we apply Mathlib theorems. To make the search efficient, we index the derivative theorems by the function they differentiate. We evaluate our approach on 500 randomly generated functions: with the index, all of them are differentiated, with a median time of 0.18\,s per function, 8.6 times faster than without the index.
item.dc:creator: Ramy Shahin

item.title: Barik transform and Barik eliminant: a novel algebraic method to solve polynomial equations in the sine and cosine of one variable
item.description: arXiv:2610.36985v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Systems of trigonometric equations appear frequently in problems related to geometry, kinematics, computer graphics, robotics, and astronomy, among many other fields. Most often these are first converted to algebraic equations via the ``tangent half-angle'' substitution and solved subsequently using various algebraic methods, such as computation of resultants. In the process, parametric singularities are introduced in the equations, and their degrees are also doubled. In this article, a novel concept call the ``Barik transform'' is introduced, which can help solve such a system without encumbering these issues, albeit only in systems that contain {\em at least} one equation of the first degree in the sine and cosine of the variable to be eliminated. It is shown how Barik transform can produce extremely compact eliminants in the closed form, without resorting to any resultant computation.
item.dc:creator: Sandipan Bandyopadhyay

item.title: GPU-Accelerated Search for Fast Matrix Multiplication over $\mathbb{F}_2$
item.description: arXiv:2609.17533v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a GPU-accelerated algorithm for searching for ways to multiply matrices with few scalar multiplications. Our algorithm searches the matrix multiplication flip graph and, on an NVIDIA H200, performs over a billion search steps per second for matrix sizes up to $7\times7$, a roughly $380\times$ improvement over previous GPU-accelerated search on the tensor for $7\times7$ matrix multiplication. We also prove that, over \(\mathbb{F}_2\), the directed matrix multiplication flip graph is strongly connected with only flip and plus edges. This removes the need for computationally expensive reduction edges in the connectivity argument used by previous work. Using this GPU-accelerated search procedure on our simplified flip graph, we find a way to multiply $7\times 7$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$ using 245 multiplications, a three-multiplication improvement over the previous record.
item.dc:creator: Zeke Medley, Anagha Gokul, Quan Luu, Panagiotis Manolios
